name: Velvet Bean
harvestProduct: green manure / grazing biomass, rolled/incorporated at late vegetative stage

evidence.quote: Velvet bean requires a long growing season and is sensitive to frost and therefore requires at least 180 frost free days.
evidence.doc: Integrated crop and pasture-based livestock production systems – Part 21: Velvet bean, SA Grain/Grain SA (Truter, Dannhauser, Smith & Trytsman), 2019

daysToHarvestRange.notes: No explicit day-count to termination found; only a calendar description ('end of February' rolling in a KZN intercrop context) and a minimum '180 frost-free days' requirement.

evidence.quote: The best method to plant velvet bean is by drilling it into the soil with about 1 m between rows and 20 cm – 80 cm between plants (20 kg/ha – 40 kg/ha seed).
evidence.doc: Integrated crop and pasture-based livestock production systems – Part 21: Velvet bean, SA Grain/Grain SA, 2019

evidence.quote: The best method to plant velvet bean is by drilling it into the soil with about 1 m between rows and 20 cm – 80 cm between plants (20 kg/ha – 40 kg/ha seed).
evidence.doc: Integrated crop and pasture-based livestock production systems – Part 21: Velvet bean, SA Grain/Grain SA, 2019

evidence.quote: Seeds are large, so seeding depth can be as deep as 10 cm but not less than 3 cm.
evidence.doc: Integrated crop and pasture-based livestock production systems – Part 21: Velvet bean, SA Grain/Grain SA, 2019

evidence.quote: 20 cm – 80 cm between plants (20 kg/ha – 40 kg/ha seed)
evidence.doc: Integrated crop and pasture-based livestock production systems – Part 21: Velvet bean, SA Grain/Grain SA, 2019

evidence.quote: Velvet bean has a high dry matter production for a subtropical legume. Yields range from 5 t/ha – 13 t/ha depending on the rainfall.
evidence.doc: Integrated crop and pasture-based livestock production systems – Part 21: Velvet bean, SA Grain/Grain SA, 2019

evidence.quote: Terminating the cover crop by rolling at a late vegetative stage (end of February).
evidence.doc: Integrated crop and pasture-based livestock production systems – Part 21: Velvet bean, SA Grain/Grain SA, 2019

zoneNotes.subtropical-coast: Requires >= 180 frost-free days and temperatures of 20-30°C (min 5°C); best suited to frost-free/mild-frost summer-rain and subtropical coastal zones such as KZN.
zoneNotes.highveld: Not suited — frost sensitivity and 180 frost-free day requirement rule out hard-frost interior.

gaps: No explicit sow-month/calendar found for any rain pattern (only a relative '45 days after companion crop' intercropping rule and a 180-frost-free-day requirement) — sowMonths left empty for all patterns.
No numeric N-fixed (kg/ha) figure found for velvet bean in any SA source.
No exact days-to-termination figure; only a qualitative 'end of February' example and general biomass/frost-day requirements.
summary: Spacing, seed rate and biomass yield (5-13 t DM/ha) are well sourced from Grain SA's Part 21 (Truter et al.). sowMonths could not be pinned to specific calendar months in any source, and no N-fixed figure or cultivar names were found, so the entry cannot reach 'ready'.
